title: Good Grooming
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Teach body changes and hygiene with care and in plain words; the class may be split for menstrual hygiene. Never point at a child.

skills.key_step: The child says the practices that keep the body clean, especially at puberty: daily bathing and clean underwear, managing sweat, gentle face washing for acne, menstrual hygiene (changing pads regularly, washing, safe disposal), clean nails, own towel and toothbrush.
representations: a calendar for changing pads (for girls)
steps: Change pads regularly and dispose of them safely.

board.do: Write "sharing a toothbrush with a friend".

misconceptions.repair: Compare hands washed with soap and without.

misconceptions.ask: How often should teeth be brushed?
misconceptions.repair: Show the plaque with a disclosing tablet if available.

misconceptions.ask: Which item should not be shared?
misconceptions.repair: Discuss how germs pass on a shared toothbrush.

misconceptions.ask: What should you do about pimples?
misconceptions.repair: Explain that squeezing pushes germs deeper and can leave scars.

listen_for: Sweat is dirty, so perfume fixes it
misconceptions.ask: Why does sweat start to smell?
misconceptions.repair: Fresh sweat after games hardly smells; stale sweat on unwashed clothes does.

checks.question: How often should underwear be changed?
Why should you not share a towel?
checks.answer: germs and skin infections pass on it
